facts.statement: Parasuchus lived during the Late Triassic period, specifically from the late Carnian to early Norian stages, in India.
facts.quote: Parasuchus is an extinct genus of basal phytosaur known from the Late Triassic (late Carnian to early Norian stage) of Telangana and Madhya Pradesh, India.

facts.statement: Richard Lydekker formally described and named Parasuchus hislopi in 1885 and proposed the family name Parasuchidae.
facts.quote: Richard Lydekker (1885) formally described and named P. hislopi, and proposed the family name Parasuchidae.

facts.statement: The original nondiagnostic holotype of Parasuchus hislopi was replaced by a neotype designated in 2001 following an application by Sankar Chatterjee.
facts.quote: To avoid additional confusion, the nondiagnostic holotype of P. hislopi was replaced by a neotype (ISI R 42) with approval from the ICZN (Opinion 2045) following the application of Chatterjee (2001).

facts.statement: Two complete, articulated skeletons with complete skulls of Parasuchus were found near the Mutapyram village in the Adilabad district.
facts.quote: Two complete and articulated skeletons that include complete skulls were collected from the Lower Maleri Formation in the vicinity of the Mutapyram village of Adilabad district.

facts.statement: The two nearly complete skeletons of Parasuchus found together were each roughly 8 feet in length.
facts.quote: Both individuals were roughly 8 ft in length, lying side by side.

facts.statement: Parasuchus hislopi had a powerful bite, estimated at 450 newtons at the front of the jaw and 1,958 newtons at the back.
facts.quote: The bite force of Parasuchus hislopi is estimated to be 450 newtons at the anterior portion of the jaw, with 1,958 newtons at the posterior portion.

facts.statement: A 2016 study placed Parasuchus hislopi within the same evolutionary group as the species Paleorhinus bransoni and Paleorhinus angustifrons.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis conducted by Kammerer et al. (2016) confirmed that Parasuchus hislopi is nested within the least inclusive clade containing the species Paleorhinus bransoni and Paleorhinus angustifrons.

facts.statement: Some researchers consider Parasuchus to be a senior synonym of the genus Paleorhinus, meaning species formerly in Paleorhinus are now placed in Parasuchus.
facts.quote: The authors thus considered the genus Parasuchus to be a senior synonym of the genus Paleorhinus (as well as Arganarhinus), and referred the species Paleorhinus bransoni, Paleorhinus angustifrons and Arganarhinus magnoculus to the genus Parasuchus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Parasuchus should be treated as a separate genus or synonymized with the genus Paleorhinus.
facts.quote: Some studies, like Chatterjee (1978) and Lucas et al. (2007), synonymized Parasuchus with another basal phytosaur, Paleorhinus.

facts.statement: The name Parasuchus comes from Greek words meaning "beside" and "Sobek," the Egyptian crocodile god.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the Greek para/παρα meaning "beside" or "near" and suchus from the Greek souchos, which refers to the Egyptian crocodile-headed god Sobek.

facts.statement: The species name hislopi honors Hislop, who drew attention to the red clay deposits near Maleri village where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: The specific name, hislopi, honors Hislop who drawn attention in 1854 to the red clays near Maleri village in which the holotype (and later the neotype and other specimens) of P. hislopi was recovered.

facts.statement: Parasuchus belongs to the family Parasuchidae.
